Samir — thanks for laying this out and for the spreadsheet. High level response below; I think we can put the detailed mapping into a one-page doc for procurement.

Quick answers:
- DNS: Redwood recommends ACME own authoritative private zones for tenant-visible FQDNs (customer-facing endpoints) but we can host stub zones for internal control-plane names. This minimizes cross-team blame and keeps TTLs under customer control.
- TLS termination: two supported patterns: 1) termination inside ACME VPC (ACME-managed edge proxy) with mutual TLS from ACME edge -> Redwood; 2) Redwood-managed edge (we terminate TLS inside our private-hosted edge in customer's VPC) using certs you provision to us. We usually recommend pattern #1 for strict isolation.
- Cert management: we accept PKCS#12 or PEM bundles. For ACME-managed termination we need a CSR proof of possession + ACME's CA thumbprint. For Redwood-managed termination we'll provide a short CSR workflow and a weekly rotation window.

Can Kimberly and her team sketch the short doc? If ACME can confirm which pattern they prefer we can assign the next steps in the MAP (mutual_action_plan).

FWIW I sketched an operational mapping and attached a diagram (edge-tls-mapping-20251121.png) plus a draft one-pager we can drop into procurement. High level notes:

- Recommended default = "customer-edge" pattern: ACME terminates public/private client connections at their managed ELB/proxy; Redwood receives mTLS to our agents. Pros: customer controls keys, simpler SOC coverage. Cons: more network config on ACME side.

- Redwood-managed edge acceptable when customers cannot run a durable proxy. In that case we must:
  * have ACME provision TLS certs to Redwood via SFTP or secure Drive (we accept PEM/PFX), or
  * Redwood can perform CSR flow with ACME's CA via our automated agent (we will need ACME to approve the CSR and provide CA signing info).

- DNS split responsibilities:
  * ACME owns tenant.* and app.* zones (customer-facing hostnames)
  * Redwood owns internal controlplane.* and hostnames used for agent scaling/backplane

- OCSP/CRL: if ACME's CA uses OCSP stapling Redwood will tolerate stapled responses; if not, Redwood needs a reachable OCSP responder from our agents in the VPC (please ensure egress rules allow that).

Next steps I propose:
1) ACME to confirm preferred pattern (customer-edge vs redwood-edge) by EOD Mon 2025-11-24
2) Laura to generate a short "Responsibility Matrix" PDF and inject it into mutual_action_plan-acme.xlsx
3) Mina to prepare the CSR/rotation checklist if ACME opts for Redwood-managed termination

Attachments: edge-tls-mapping-20251121.png (diagram), mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx (MAP draft).

Thanks — Kim
